title: Euclid telescope spots oldest quasars ever discovered, adding to "perplexing" space mystery
facts: An international team of astronomers discovered 31 ancient quasars using the European Space Agency's Euclid telescope.
The Euclid space telescope operates at a stable hovering position approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.
The group of 31 newly discovered quasars includes the two oldest quasars ever observed.
Light from the two oldest discovered quasars originated when the universe was approximately 670 million years old.
The current estimated age of the universe is 13.8 billion years.
The recent Euclid telescope discovery beats the previous 2021 record for the oldest known quasar by approximately 20 million years.
The European Space Agency launched the Euclid space telescope in 2023.
The Euclid telescope doubled the number of ancient quasars known to science within two years of operation.
Daming Yang is the lead author of the Euclid quasar study published in Astronomy & Astrophysics.
The newly discovered quasars date back to the epoch of reionization in cosmic history.
The James Webb space telescope also conducted recent observations of the newly announced ancient quasars.
The Euclid telescope captured a highly detailed image containing 60 million stars at the center of the Milky Way galaxy.
The Euclid telescope captured an image of the Abell 2390 galaxy cluster encompassing more than 50,000 galaxies in 2024.
The Abell 2390 galaxy cluster is located 2.7 billion light years away from Earth.
The Euclid space telescope was launched from Cape Canaveral atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket.
